(1) The only credentialed step is the combined `run: npm ci && npm publish`. Moving NPM_TOKEN to 'step-level env on the steps that use them' therefore still exposes it to every dependency lifecycle/install script that `npm ci` runs, which is a third-party code path on its own. The draft should recommend splitting install from publish, using `npm ci --ignore-scripts` where possible, and giving the token only to the publish step. (2) No step in release.yml uses CLOUD_DEPLOY_KEY. The file has no deploy step, even though the request says the workflow deploys. The draft never notices this, so it misses the simplest control: remove CLOUD_DEPLOY_KEY from this job, or move it to a separate deploy job behind a protected environment. It also leaves unresolved the gap between the request ('deploys to our cloud account') and the file. (3) actions/checkout@v4 persists GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config by default, so any later step (including the unreviewed restore-cache.sh) can read it. `persist-credentials: false` is not mentioned.
